subject: science
skillName: Rock Layers and Fossils Show Change

items.prompt:
In stacked rock layers, the oldest layer is usually
A) at the top
B) at the bottom
C) in the middle only
D) missing

steps: New layers form on top, so the bottom is oldest.

items.prompt:
Fossils are
A) living animals
B) preserved remains or traces of living things
C) types of rocks with no life
D) clouds
items.answer: B) preserved remains or traces of living things

steps: Fossils are preserved remains or traces of once-living things.

items.prompt:
Finding fish fossils in a dry desert suggests the area once had
A) water
B) no life
C) only sand
D) fire

steps: Fish fossils mean the area used to be underwater.

items.prompt:
The youngest rock layer is usually found
A) at the bottom
B) at the top
C) outside the cliff
D) underground only

steps: The top layer formed most recently.

items.prompt:
Rock layers are like a record of time because
A) each layer formed at a different time
B) they are all the same age
C) they have no order
D) they never change
items.answer: A) each layer formed at a different time

items.prompt:
A layer of ocean shells lies below a layer of tree fossils. Which formed first?
A) The shell layer
B) The tree layer
C) They formed at the same time
D) Neither formed

steps: Lower layers form first, so the shell layer is older.

items.prompt:
A cliff has ocean fossils below and land fossils above. This is evidence that the area
A) was always a desert
B) changed from ocean to dry land over time
C) never changed
D) changed from land to ocean
items.answer: B) changed from ocean to dry land over time

steps: The older ocean layer and younger land layer show the shift from sea to land.

items.prompt:
Fish fossils found high in a mountain are evidence that the rock was once
A) on the Moon
B) underwater
C) on fire
D) in space

steps: Fish fossils show the area was once covered by water.
